newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Aid workers say Rwanda commandos in east Zaire town.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers say Rwanda commandos in east Zaire town.

text.p: Western aid workers said they had reports on Wednesday that Rwandan commandos had entered the eastern Zaire lakeside town of Bukavu just over the border from Rwanda and had driven Zairean troops out of it.

"We have field reports that Bukavu has fallen and that Rwandan commandos are now there, but we have no independent confirmation," said one aid worker currently in Geneva. Western agencies have pulled out of Bukavu because of lack of security.

The aid workers had no other details. There have been no credible eyewitness accounts of the fighting in the region which has uprooted half a million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fleeing fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels.
Tensions were running dangerously high along the border on Wednesday after gunbattles between Zairean and Rwandan troops and a Rwandan military sortie into Zairean territory.

Earlier, Rwandan Lieutenant-Colonel Firmin Kagame told reporters in Rwanda's border town of Cyangugu that he sent "a good-sized" force of troops into Zaire after nightfall on Tuesday in retaliation for Zairean firing into Rwanda.
"After they hit our territory and injured and killed our people and hit civilians we were forced to retaliate," the commander said.
"We retaliated by two means," he added. "We fired at them with heavy machineguns and mortars and we sent in a force to destabilise them and to force them away from where they could affect us."
In the Rwandan capital Kigali, Vice-President and Defence Minister Paul Kagame told a news conference that his country would have to respond if faced with what he called "Zairean aggression".
"If Zaire brings the war to us we shall fight Zaire. That is not a big problem for me. We are ready to fight even though we seek no war with Zaire," Kagame said.
Rwanda's minority Tutsi rulers, who took power after Hutu-led genocide of their fellow tribesmen in 1994, feel persecuted and surrounded by majority Hutus.

One million Rwandan Hutus fled to eastern Zaire in fear of reprisal for the genocide and militiamen among them kept the military threat alive with cross-border raids into Rwanda from camps just outside Rwandan borders.
Many soldiers of Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army grew up in neighbouring Zaire, Burundi and Uganda and would be equally at home across the borders.
